A private fishing journal

Your fishing life is worth remembering.

Keep your trips, catches, places, photos, routes, and notes together in a journal that belongs to you. No profile to build, no feed, nobody keeping score.

No account required. Start writing things down, then come back years later through your own history, your year in recap, and photo books made from the days you kept.

View on the App Store ↗See how it works
01 · The whole day

The day is bigger than the catch.

You remember more than the fish. The lake before sunrise. The stretch of river you keep going back to. The friend who came along. The lure that finally worked. The weather turning. The one that got away.

Cast Your Line gives those details a place to stay.

02 · On the water

Pick a water and start fishing. The rest is optional.

Recording a trip takes a few taps, so it never gets in the way of the fishing. Log fish as they come, or fill in the details on the drive home.

Keep it connected

Keep the whole trip together.

Start with the day, then let the rest of it attach: the catches and the species, the photos, the water, the weather, the setup you brought, the person in the other seat, the bait that finally worked.

Keep the photo, the place, the person beside you, and the notes you will want years from now all attached to the same day, instead of scattered across a camera roll and three other apps.

Illustration · Blue Mesa Reservoir
03 · Routes and places

Remember where the day took you.

Turn on optional GPS route tracking when you want a record of your movement through a place. Follow a river on foot. Walk a shoreline. Paddle a lake. Troll from a boat.

Years later, a line on a map brings back things a place name cannot: the bend where you kept stopping, the shallow side you waded, the long crossing before the wind picked up.

Explore GPS and maps →

04 · Explore

Wander back through your own history.

Every trip you record ends up in Explore. Open the calendar and see the days you were out, how many fish each one brought, and which ones held a first or a personal best. Browse your catches, your species, your waters, and your photos. Jump back a year, or three.

It is not a dashboard. It is a way to wonder when that was, and find out.

See Explore and history →
Annual recaps

Your year on the water, brought back to life.

One trip you can hold in your head. A whole year is harder. By winter you might remember four or five days clearly and lose the rest, even the good ones.

A yearly recap puts the season back together. Your biggest fish. The day they would not stop biting. The busiest month. The water you kept returning to, and the new water you tried. The species you caught for the first time. Who came with you. Your favorite trip, in the words you wrote about it.

Nothing is ranked and nobody wins it. It is simply the year you actually had, handed back to you.

See recaps and history →
05 · Photo books

Turn a year of fishing into something you can keep.

All season you are saving photos, notes, places, and catches without thinking much about it. A photo book is where that ends up. Cast Your Line lays your year out as a book: a map of the waters you fished, the year month by month in pictures, a page for each outing, every species you caught, and a logbook of every trip at the back.

You choose what goes in: the outings, the photos, the page size, and whether your notes and the people you fished with are included. Then you get a PDF. Print it at home, or hand the file to a print shop and get a bound copy back. One for the shelf. One for the person who was in the boat with you.

See how a year becomes a book →

No scoreboard required

Some trips are worth remembering even when nothing bites.

Some days are about the place. Some are about the person who came with you. Some are quiet mornings you needed more than you realized. Cast Your Line gives all of them a place in your fishing history.

06 · Personal by design

Your journal does not need an audience.

Plenty of people enjoy fishing apps built around other people. This one is built around you. There is nothing to post and nothing to keep up with.

  • Your journal stays on your devices and in your own iCloud
  • No account required
  • No ads
  • No notifications
  • No public profile
  • No social feed
  • No followers and no likes
  • No leaderboard to chase
  • No expectation that you share anything

If you never mention to a single person that you keep this journal, it works exactly the same.

Learn about privacy →
07 · Over the years

More meaningful every year.

One trip is useful. A season starts to tell a story. Five years in, you can see the places you keep coming back to, the people who show up again and again in the photos, and how your fishing quietly changed without anyone announcing it.

You only write a trip down once. The same day turns up again in your calendar, your catches and species, your waters, the recap for that month and that year, and the photo book you make at the end of the season.

Every year you fish gets its own page. The current one fills in as you go.
